proposal.hypothesis: This remains a one-way 16-byte SIMD-prefix/scalar-suffix hybrid, not T1-style whole-buffer validation. The selected parent locates the first high-bit lane in a mixed vector before calling the scalar decoder. Since that vector starts at a known code-point boundary and the scalar decoder already skips ASCII, starting it at the vector boundary may avoid the mask-shifting lane search at the cost of rechecking at most 15 ASCII bytes. The first high-bit byte remains input to strict validation, including when it is a stray continuation. Prior timings motivate the contrast but do not establish its cause; measure on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and official ASCII/malformed boundary checks.

retained: Remove the bit-by-bit search for the first high-bit lane; when a complete 16-byte SIMD block contains any high bit, invoke the strict scalar decoder from that block's known code-point boundary.
Skip only complete 16-byte blocks confirmed entirely ASCII; leave tails within n to the scalar decoder and retain exact UTF-8 validity behavior, ABI, output, and thread budget.
